guarantees.claim: Shadowed register fields in cfg_shadowed and entropy_refresh_threshold_shadowed output storage and update error signals (err_update, err_storage) to the enclosing design, but this chunk does not react to them internally.

Write accesses to cfg_shadowed, entropy_period, entropy_refresh_threshold_shadowed, key_share0, key_share1, key_len, and prefix registers are gated by cfg_regwen_qs: the internal gated_we signal equals the raw we AND cfg_regwen_qs, preventing writes when cfg_regwen_qs is 0.
guarantees.cond: any write attempt to the listed registers

guarantees.claim: Interrupt enable bits (intr_enable.kmac_done, intr_enable.fifo_empty, intr_enable.kmac_err) are driven solely by software; hardware does not update them because de is tied to 0 and d to '0 in the prim_subreg instances.

The intr_test_qe and cmd_qe signals are asserted only when all individual field write-enable signals (flds_we) of the respective registers are active simultaneously, producing a one-cycle qualified enable pulse.
guarantees.cond: on register write with all fields activated in the same cycle

guarantees.claim: The kmac_err field in intr_state uses SwAccessW1C, guaranteeing that a write of 1 to this bit clears it, while a write of 0 leaves it unchanged, as enforced by the prim_subreg primitive.
guarantees.cond: when intr_state_we is active and intr_state_kmac_err_wd is 1

guarantees.claim: The key_len register is instantiated with SwAccessWO and its qs output is left unconnected, guaranteeing that the written value cannot be read back via the register interface.

The cfg_shadowed_qe signal is generated by a flip-flop that samples the AND of all cfg_shadowed_flds_we bits; if any field has not been written in the current cycle, cfg_shadowed_qe remains 0, preventing a partial shadow register update commit.
guarantees.cond: on any write to cfg_shadowed fields

assumptions.claim: The top-level design must monitor and respond to the shadow register error signals (err_update, err_storage) from cfg_shadowed and entropy_refresh_threshold_shadowed because this chunk itself performs no error handling or fault containment.
assumptions.cond: any shadow register update or storage error
assumptions.risk: If ignored, critical configuration corruption (e.g., mode, key length, entropy settings) could occur without detection, leading to security failures.

assumptions.claim: Software must comply with the W1C clearing protocol for intr_state.kmac_err; writing a 0 to this bit does not clear it, so incorrect software may leave the interrupt pending.
assumptions.risk: Missed interrupt clearing could cause spurious or lost interrupts, leading to stuck alert or failure to detect subsequent errors.

assumptions.claim: cfg_regwen_qs must reflect a trusted write-enable state and must only be set to 1 by authorized software; if it is accidentally or maliciously set to 1, the gated write protection on sensitive registers is defeated.
assumptions.risk: Unauthorized modification of key material, configuration, or entropy settings, potentially compromising cryptographic operations.

assumptions.claim: rst_shadowed_ni must be properly asserted and deasserted relative to the system reset sequence; the chunk assumes a correctly sequenced reset for the shadowed register primitives.
assumptions.risk: Improper shadow reset could leave shadow registers in an unknown state, bypassing the write-once-check and causing silent corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: The key share registers key_share0 and key_share1 (512 bits each) are instantiated without any explicit clear-on-lock, clear-on-reset, or clear-on-disable mechanism in this chunk. If the wider design does not implement a wipe, secret key material may persist after the module is locked or deactivated.
uncertain_points.cond: after configuration lock (cfg_regwen_qs→0) or module disable
uncertain_points.risk: Key leakage through post-operational readout or scan chains, violating zeroization requirements.

uncertain_points.claim: The entropy_seed register is writeable via entropy_seed_we without being gated by cfg_regwen_qs (line 1400), unlike other sensitive registers. This may allow an attacker to inject chosen entropy values after the module has been locked, subverting entropy quality guarantees.
uncertain_points.risk: Weakening of cryptographic operations through predictable or zeroed entropy leading to key recovery or loss of randomness.

uncertain_points.claim: The shadow register error signals (err_update, err_storage) are exposed but unused locally. It must be verified in the integration layer that they are connected to the alert or fault handling logic; otherwise, corruption of critical registers (e.g., mode, sideload) goes undetected.
uncertain_points.cond: any shadow register access resulting in an error
uncertain_points.risk: Silent acceptance of tampered or corrupted shadow register values, breaking hardware-enforced configuration integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: The msg_mask field in cfg_shadowed is labeled 'msg_mask', suggesting a message masking function. Its exact security semantics (e.g., whether it is a boolean mask enable or a mask value) are not clear from this chunk alone; misconfiguration could bypass message integrity or secrecy.
uncertain_points.risk: Masked message data might leak sensitive information unintentionally if the mask is not applied correctly or if the field has a different meaning than expected.

uncertain_points.claim: The en_unsupported_modestrength field in cfg_shadowed allows software to enable an unsupported mode/strength combination. There is no local hardware check that the requested combination is actually supported; validation may be deferred to the KMAC core, which could lead to undefined behavior if not handled.
uncertain_points.cond: when en_unsupported_modestrength is set to 1 and unsupported mode/strength is selected
uncertain_points.risk: Potential functional failure, denial-of-service, or unexpected security properties if the core does not reject the configuration.

uncertain_points.claim: The shadow register commitment (cfg_shadowed_qe) depends on the AND of all flds_we bits being true in the same cycle. If software writes fields in multiple cycles, the AND will never fire. It must be confirmed that the software interface ensures a single-cycle write for the entire register group to prevent a permanent lockout.
uncertain_points.cond: when software performs partial writes to cfg_shadowed fields
uncertain_points.risk: Shadow register update stall; configuration never takes effect, potentially leaving the module in an unconfigured or insecure state.
